work_completed: Audited the whole repository before modifying anything and classified modules, packages, scripts, configuration and dependencies into the seven requested classes (docs/space-runtime/audit-and-classification.md). Nothing was deleted, archived or moved

Found that the fusion core (FusionEngine, ReadinessAssessor, ModelFusionEngine, state feed) has no HTTP surface anywhere: backend/app/routers/fusion.py fabricates readiness with random.uniform, and apps/api exposes hard-coded advocates

Built the Space runtime in spaces/ai-fusion/: Docker SDK image (python 3.11, non-root uid 1000, HEALTHCHECK), minimal 3-package requirements, lifespan startup/shutdown, non-secret configuration logging, and a payload assembler that copies the runtime subset from GitHub instead of forking src/

Exposed the cognitive core at stable versioned paths: /v1/fusion/{agents,readiness,attempt,state-feed}, /v1/sessions/{run,demo-run} reusing services.api.app.session_service, /v1/runtime/info, plus /health and /readyz with real dependency checks
Mounted src.fusion.agent_loop_http.create_app verbatim so the nlt.agent-loop.v1 seam keeps its tested behaviour (registry allow-list, one-in-flight 429, timeout quarantine 503, fail-closed 4xx)

Implemented ASFDK governance context carriage: agent identity, session, provenance, governance version and capabilities in headers, enforced by default with structured 403s; permissive mode is local-only and always labelled governance_enforced=false
Wrote spaces/ai-fusion/tests/test_runtime.py (20 integration tests) covering health, governance denials, fusion routes, session orchestration and the mounted contract seam

Documented architecture and boundaries, including eight architectural conflicts (three overlapping API surfaces, a latent broken import in apps/api, fabricated readiness in backend/app, unwired NPC module, TOI version drift, unqueued training pipeline, ungoverned contract seam, physics fields in the state feed) reported rather than silently resolved
blockers: The Space cannot be deployed from this session: divergent-tech/Ai-fusion is still in NO_APP_FILE state and this agent's Hugging Face access is read-only (no HF tool registered for the connection, no HF_TOKEN in the environment). Payload assembly, local execution and verification are complete; the upload step needs either HF write tooling or a token with write scope
decisions_made: Chose a Docker Space over Gradio: the deliverable is a service interface for the API platform and Godot, and Gradio would introduce a UI framework the repository does not use

Deployed a runtime subset assembled at deploy time (src/, app/, services/api/app session service) rather than committing a second copy of src/ under spaces/, so the Space cannot drift from GitHub and no source is duplicated
Defaulted FUSION_AGENT_LOOP_MODEL to baseline so the Space boots with no checkpoint; gguf/transformers stay available and fail at startup when misconfigured, as the contract documentation requires
Left ModelFusionEngine and the training trigger unexposed: TrainingPipeline.run_async starts a bare thread with no queue or durable run state, so an HTTP trigger would misrepresent capability
Did not touch any file outside spaces/ai-fusion/ and docs/space-runtime/ except a .gitignore entry for the local verification venv
